# Where is it hottest?

## Row

### Column {width="60%"}

::: {.card title="Surface temperature and tree cover by neighbourhood"}
Interactive LSOA map goes here, with surface temperature and tree cover as layers you switch between.

Satellites measure how hot surfaces get, not the air people feel. Tree cover data are from 2013.
:::

### Column {width="40%"}

::: {.card title="Are the hottest neighbourhoods the most deprived?"}
Scatter of temperature against deprivation goes here.
:::

::: {.card title="Hot days per year since 1960"}
Line chart of days above 25°C goes here.
:::

# Where do they overlap?
## Row {height="65%"}

### Column {width="70%"}

::: {.card title="Where heat and at-risk residents overlap"}
Interactive bivariate map goes here, with care homes and cool spaces as points you can switch on and off.

This shows where hot neighbourhoods and at-risk residents coincide, not which residents are actually exposed.
:::

### Column {width="30%"}

::: {.card title="How to read the map"}
3×3 bivariate legend goes here, plus one sentence on what the darkest corner means.
:::

::: {.card title="Hot neighbourhoods with many at-risk residents"}
Priority list goes here: neighbourhood, heat level, at-risk level, distance to nearest cool space.
